original_question: Fix a klt pair (X, Delta). Is there a positive constant epsilon such that for every (K_X + Delta)-nonnegative birational map X --> X' and every point x in X', the normalized volume vol-hat(x, X', Delta') is at least epsilon?
target_in_paper: Problem 29 in Section 4 (the MMP/local-volume question in the paper's miscellaneous questions section), not Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core mathematical content of the paper's Problem 29 essentially correctly: fix a klt pair, ask for a uniform positive lower bound on normalized volumes on every birational model obtained by a (K_X+\Delta)-nonnegative birational map, uniformly over points x\in X'. It also correctly uses the transformed boundary \Delta' and the normalized volume invariant \widehat{\mathrm{vol}}.
missing_details: The paper places this question in the setting of a projective klt pair of log general type; equivalently, K_X+\Delta is big. Your draft omits this hypothesis and is therefore broader than the paper.
The ambient setting is characteristic 0 (in the paper's K-stability/MMP context, over an algebraically closed field, typically \mathbb{C}).
The constant should be written as \varepsilon=\varepsilon(X,\Delta)>0, i.e. depending only on the fixed pair.
One should specify that X' is a normal projective birational model and that \Delta' is the strict (birational) transform of \Delta on X'.
The quantifier should be over closed points x\in X' (normalized volume is defined pointwise for klt singularities, and smooth points are allowed as well).
The phrase '(K_X+\Delta)-nonnegative birational map' should be made explicit, for example: on a common resolution p:W\to X and q:W\to X', one has p^*(K_X+\Delta)\le q^*(K_{X'}+\Delta').
It should be explicit that \widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X',\Delta') means the normalized volume of the klt germ x\in (X',\Delta').

The nearby paper context is MMP: the question asks whether the lower bound persists uniformly on all models reachable from (X,\Delta) by (K_X+\Delta)-nonnegative birational modifications, rather than on arbitrary unrelated birational models.
refined_question:
Let (X,\Delta) be a projective klt pair of log general type over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. Does there exist a constant \varepsilon=\varepsilon(X,\Delta)>0 such that for every (K_X+\Delta)-nonnegative birational map \phi\colon X\dashrightarrow X' to a normal projective variety, with \Delta' the strict transform of \Delta on X', and for every closed point x\in X', one has
\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X',\Delta')\ge \varepsilon?
Here '(K_X+\Delta)-nonnegative' means that on a common resolution p\colon W\to X and q\colon W\to X' one has p^*(K_X+\Delta)\le q^*(K_{X'}+\Delta').
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper's later MMP/local-volume problem, namely Problem 29, rather than the introductory Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3. The closest paper-faithful sharpening is therefore to keep the same question but restore the hypotheses and hidden notation from the surrounding discussion: the pair is of log general type, the map is understood in the standard MMP sense of (K_X+\Delta)-nonnegativity, \Delta' is the birational transform, and the lower bound is asked uniformly over all closed points on all such birational models. The nearby context is the local-to-global lower bound for normalized volume on the original model and the question of whether such a bound survives along the general-type MMP; this is why broadening from log general type to arbitrary klt pairs would drift away from the paper's actual intent.
